title: Homogeneous Refusals: Do All Models Share the Same Over- and Under-Refusal Blind Spots?

original_idea.body:
# Homogeneous Refusals: Do All Models Share the Same Over- and Under-Refusal Blind Spots?

**Problem:** If the refusal boundary is homogeneous across providers, the same benign use cases are blocked everywhere and the same harmful edge cases slip through everywhere.

**Direction:** Use an over-refusal benchmark slice plus a harmful-edge set. Query 6+ open models, classify refuse/comply, and measure inter-model agreement on the refusal boundary vs chance independence.

**Why it matters:** A shared refusal blind spot is a society-wide blind spot; measuring correlation (not just per-model rates) is the novel contribution.

**Relevant context:** Artificial Hivemind; XSTest; correlated-errors framing.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: correlated over/under-refusal across providers is a concrete fleet-wide safety gap (harmful edge cases no provider catches).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Existing refusal benchmarks + classify refuse/comply across models + correlation; accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: inter-model agreement on refusal boundary vs chance, clear metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Correlation-focused refusal audit labs deprioritize; public models, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference over benchmark slices, one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Over-refusal benchmarks exist; measuring cross-model correlation of the boundary may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Over-refusal benchmarks exist; measuring cross-model correlation of the boundary may be open.
